name: Finite Chain Detachment Expectation
problem_statement: A polymer is confined to a narrow planar trench and follows a prescribed right-angle “staircase” of N=20 unit segments (d=1.00). Its rightmost endpoint is fixed at P_0 = (8.00, 0.00). Moving inward along the chain from this end, the segment directions alternate between a unit step in -x and a unit step in +y (starting with -x for the first segment). Segments can detach only in order from the right end, so at any instant the set of detached segments is a single contiguous block of length n in {0,1,...,20}. Detaching a segment costs energy epsilon = 1.70. Each detached segment has g=3 internal microstates, whereas each attached segment has one. The two free ends are joined by a frictionless ring connected to an ideal force source that maintains a constant tension of magnitude f=0.70 along the direction of the taut free polymer. The ring’s location is fixed at a clamp point A = (15.00, 0.00). For a given n, the free polymer between A and the peel front is taut and takes the shortest possible path in the plane from A to the peel front that does not enter a smooth circular exclusion region (a post) of radius R = 1.20 centered at (10.00, 3.50). What is the expected number of detached segments <n>, in thermal equilibrium for this finite chain?

name: Josephson Array Free Energy
problem_statement: A long 1D Josephson junction array supports phase slips that can nucleate only from the right end, so the allowed macrostates are indexed by a single integer n >= 0 (the rightmost n junctions have slipped). The n=0 state has energy 0. Each additional slip has a core energy cost epsilon. Each slipped junction contributes a factor g of internal microstates; unslipped junctions have one. Biasing: the array is connected to a common reference node by two ideal current sources. The right source injects a current +I from the reference node into the right pad; the left source injects a current -I from the reference node into the left pad (so the array current is I from right to left). Let the instantaneous pad voltages relative to the reference node be V_R(t) and V_L(t). Due to the symmetric bias network, during a phase-slip voltage pulse the pad voltages satisfy V_R(t) = -V_L(t) for all t. A single phase slip advances the gauge-invariant phase difference between pads by 2*pi, so by the Josephson relation the integrated array voltage obeys integral from -inf to inf of (V_R(t)-V_L(t))dt = Phi_0, where Phi_0 = 2.067833848e-15 V*s. Define the electrical work delivered by the sources to the array during a slip event by the signed power convention W = integral from -inf to inf of (I_R V_R(t) + I_L V_L(t))dt. Assume parameters such that runaway does not occur. Constants: epsilon = 3.90e-22 J (corrected for bound regime), I = 75.0 nA, g = 5, T = 9.00 K. What is the Helmholtz free energy F(T) of the array relative to the fully unslipped state in the bound regime? Give the final answer in Joules, rounded to 3 significant figures.

name: Scattering Amplitude Constant
problem_statement: We examine the high-energy limit (sqrt(s) >> M_W) of the scattering process d_R + dbar_L -> W_L- + W_L+. In the simplified electroweak theory provided: Vertices: The photon couples to quarks with V_gamma_qq = +i(e/3)gamma^mu and to W-bosons with the standard Yang-Mills vertex. Helicity: The incoming d_R state forbids the t-channel diagram, isolating the s-channel photon diagram. Polarization: The outgoing longitudinal W-bosons are approximated by epsilon_L^mu(k) approx k^mu / M_W. As s -> infinity, the leading behavior of the total scattering amplitude M_total can be written in the form: M_total approx i * K * (e^2 / M_W^2 * s * sin(theta)) where K is a dimensionless real number. What is the exact value of K? Give your answer as a decimal rounded to three decimal places.

name: PT-Symmetric Parity Im(P12)
problem_statement: A two-mode gain/loss device evolves as i*d/dt(psi)=H*psi in the basis psi=(a_L,a_R)^T, with H=[[i*gamma, kappa*e^(i*theta)], [kappa*e^(-i*theta), -i*gamma]] where gamma>0, kappa>0, and theta in R. Time reversal is complex conjugation T(psi)=psi*, so PT symmetry means P H* P = H. In this phase-coupled system, T inverts the phase parameter theta. A valid parity operator P must satisfy P_dag=P and P^2=I. Impose the convention that P(theta) depends continuously on theta and satisfies P(0)=[[0,1],[1,0]]. Fix theta=pi/3. What is Im(P_12)? (Give answer as a decimal rounded to 3 places, i.e., sqrt(3)/2).

name: Rotating Wire Action
problem_statement: A rigid straight wire is welded to a rotor that spins with constant angular velocity Omega=3 rad/s about a fixed axis A (not vertical). The axis A lies in the x-z plane and is tilted by beta=30 degrees away from the vertical Z axis. The closest-approach distance between the wire and the axis A is A=1m at a point P. At P, the wire makes an angle theta=60 degrees with the horizontal plane, and the wire is oriented so that moving upward along the wire has a horizontal component in the direction of the rotor’s motion at P. A particle of mass m=2kg moves along the wire with a constant relative speed s_dot=2m/s. What is the action S = integral from 0 to 1 of L dt, expressed to 3 decimal places in Joule-seconds?

name: Möbius Pendulum Precession
problem_statement: A space station is constructed with a centerline radius R and a track forming a Möbius strip. A transporter pod travels along the centerline at constant speed v. Twist: As the pod completes one full loop (2*pi*R), the floor normal n rotates continuously by pi radians (180 deg) about the tangent t. Experiment: A Foucault pendulum is suspended inside. At t=0, it oscillates in the transverse direction b. The pod completes one full loop. Consider only non-holonomic transport and Coriolis effects. What is the magnitude of the angle Delta_theta between the pendulum's plane of oscillation and the transverse axis of the pod's floor at the moment of return? (Answer in radians, i.e., pi).

name: Superconducting Ring Max Cooper Speed
problem_statement: A superconducting toroidal ring (R=2.5mm, sigma=0.5um^2) rotates at Omega about z. A Josephson junction (Ic=1.8649uA) is present. ns(theta)=n0(1+eps*cos(theta)), eps=0.6, L_geo=200pH, n0=5.58e27 m^-3. Ramp Omega quasistatically from 0. What is the maximum lab-frame tangential speed v_max of the Cooper pairs anywhere on the ring (in m/s) at the instant the n=0 metastable minimum disappears?

name: Interceptor Asymptotic Distance
problem_statement: Interceptor D (V=12m/s) pursues target T (u=12m/s) with a clockwise-biased pursuit (alpha=20 deg). Initial positions: T(0)=(0,0), D(0)=(130, -450). Switch event: The interceptor switches to pure pursuit (alpha=0) at the first time t_s > 0 when the bearing rate phi_dot = 0. What is the asymptotic distance r_inf = limit as t->inf of r(t) in meters? (3 sig figs)

name: Bead on Accelerating Wire
problem_statement: A bead of mass m slides without friction on a rigid wire bolted to a carriage accelerating at a = a0(cos(phi)x + sin(phi)y). a0=6.20m/s^2, phi=25 deg, wire rotated by theta=30 deg. Wire geometry: V=f(S) where S=|U|. Segment I: f(S)=6*S^2.5 (0 < S < 0.35). Segment II: f(S) is C1 at 0.35, k2=-262.635m^-2. Bead released from S=0. What is the bead's maximum horizontal displacement magnitude |delta_x_max| (in meters, 3 s.f.) from the release point before it turns around, measured along the lab x-axis?

name: Topological Film Max Wavelength
problem_statement: A 20nm film of a 3D topological insulator (bulk D3d, surface C3v) at cryogenic temp. Normal incidence laser (z-axis, 443nm). Detector co-linear. Relevant singlet levels: Bulk: B0(A1g) 0.0eV, B1(A2u) 2.80eV, B2(Eu) 3.24eV, B3(A2u) 4.70eV, B4(A1g) 5.60eV. Surface: S0(A1) 0.0eV, S1(A1) 2.14eV, S2(E) 3.24eV. B2 and S2 hybridize: H+ 3.29eV (90% B2), H- 3.19eV (10% B2). What is the maximum wavelength (nm, 3 s.f.) detectable by the photodetector?

name: Nitrate Ion Max Wavelength
problem_statement: A planar nitrate ion (D3h) at cryogenic temp. 325nm laser incident along z-axis. Detector co-linear. Singlets: S0(A1') 0eV, S1(A2'') 3.82eV, S2(E') 5.06eV, S3(E'') 6.30eV, S4(A1') 7.64eV. What is the maximum wavelength (nm, 3 s.f.) detectable by the photodetector along the z-axis?

name: Order g4 Integrand Value
problem_statement: Toy QFT: scalars A,B,C, Lint = -gABC. connected 2->2 (A+A->A+A) at lowest nonvanishing order. m_A=0.5GeV, m_B=0, m_C=M->0. k1=(1, sqrt(3)/2, 0, 0), k2=(1, -sqrt(3)/2, 0, 0), k3=(-1, -sqrt(3)/4, -3/4, 0), k4=(-1, sqrt(3)/4, 3/4, 0). Loop momentum q0=(0.3, 0.2, -0.1, 0.4)GeV. g=1.00. Using standard measure d^4q/(2*pi)^4, what is the numerical value of the integrand I(q0) in GeV^-4 (4 s.f.)?

name: Surface-Phonon Max Wavelength
problem_statement: 3D TI thin film (D3d bulk, C3v surface). Co-linear laser/detector on z-axis. Laser lambda=420.271nm. Levels: B0-B4, S0-S3. H_hi(4.01eV) and H_lo(3.20eV) hybridize from B2/S2. Efficient surface-phonon channel: H_hi(E) -> S3(A2) via phonon (E). Radiative H_hi -> H_lo forbidden. What is the max wavelength (nm, 3 s.f.) detected on-axis?

name: PT-Symmetric Reflection Ratio
problem_statement: Non-Hermitian potential V(x) = i*lambda*delta(x) - i*lambda*delta(x-L). u = m*lambda/(hbar^2 * k) = 0.5. Phase k*L = pi/2. R_L and R_R are reflection coefficients from left/right. System is PT-symmetric. What is the numerical value of the ratio |R_L|/|R_R|?

name: Anion Membane Max Wavelength
problem_statement: Planar triatomic anion (D3h) in membrane. 352nm laser along z-axis. Levels: S0(A1'), S1(A2'') 3.52eV, S2(E') 4.81eV, S3(E'') 5.44eV, S4(A1') 7.04eV. What is the maximum wavelength (nm, 3 s.f.) detected along the z-axis?

name: Relativistic Projectile Speed
problem_statement: Rigid tube L0=1.5m. Projectile frame length l0=1.2m. Compressive signal u_f=0.6c, tensile recoil u_b=0.4c. Tip halts if compressive signal from flange reaches it OR tensile signal from tip reaches flange before compressive reaches tip. What is minimum speed V_min (m/s, 3 s.f.) for puncture?

name: Sphere Drone Bearing Angle
problem_statement: Spherical drone on R=2m sphere. Constant angle alpha with e_theta toward e_phi. v=0.25m/s. theta_0=0.5rad. Reaches theta_max < pi and reverses. Crosses initial meridian twice. Total arc-length L=19.7392m between crossings at phi=2pi and 4pi. What is alpha in degrees?

name: Maximum Likelihood Bearing
problem_statement: Rhumb-runner drone on R=2m sphere. v=0.25m/s. alpha constant. theta_0=0.5. Crosses meridian at 2pi, 4pi, 6pi. Arc-lengths measured with 0.05m noise: L12=19.503, L23=19.441. What is the MLE of alpha in degrees?

name: Proper Time on Rotating Sphere
problem_statement: Clock-bot on R=2m sphere, v=0.25m/s, alpha=60 deg. theta_0=0.5. Sphere rotates at Omega=1.0 rad/s. c=50m/s. What is the proper time delta_tau elapsed between phi=0 and 2pi (seconds, 4 s.f.)?

name: Total Rapidity psi_tot
problem_statement: 3 inertial frames S, S', S''. (c*dt)^2 - (dx)^2 = (9m)^2 in S. Lightcone x+ = ct+x, x- = ct-x. S'' has dx''=0 (same position). In S', delta_x'+ / delta_x'- = 7. What is the total rapidity psi_tot = psi_1 + psi_2 between S and S'' (3 s.f.)?

name: Reflected Photon Frequency
problem_statement: Infinite plane mirror in S1 (V=0.8c along x). Source in S2 (V=0.6c along y). Photon emitted in S2 with f0=6.00e14 Hz at theta=45 deg. Specular reflection in S1. What is the frequency f_det in Hz detected back in S2? (3 s.f.)

name: Collision Opening Angle
problem_statement: Solenoidal spectrometer B=(kappa)I. Elastic collision of identical species at z=0. B(z<0) I=8A, B(z>0) I=12A. Incoming helix: r=0.6m, dz=6m after 5 turns. Outgoing 1: r=0.25m, dz=3.2m after 4 turns. Outgoing 2: r=0.28m, dz=1.8m after 3 turns. What is the lab-frame opening angle delta in degrees between the two outgoing velocity vectors?

name: Lorentz Scalar a*a
problem_statement: Micro-probe receding along +x. f_rec(t)/f_star = e^(-t/T), T=5.0s. c=3e8 m/s. What is the Lorentz scalar 4-acceleration a*a in m^2/s^4 at lab time t=3.0s? (3 s.f.)

name: Parent Lab Energy
problem_statement: Neutral X0 (497.611 MeV) decays to pi+ pi- (139.57 MeV). isotropic in rest frame. Detector sees pions with theta <= 60 deg. Ratio of max to min recorded pion energies is alpha=3.00. What is the parent energy Ex in MeV? (1 decimal place)

name: Ballast Transfer Rise Time
problem_statement: Capsule in bore tube filled with water. m_s=120g, m_b=90g, V=210 cm^3. Ballast transfers at 1.5g/s between chambers at +/- 40mm. Tube flipped at t=0. Static friction mu_s=0.35. Wedged tilt sin(theta)=2*delta/L. How long after the flip (seconds, 3 s.f.) does the capsule first move upward?

name: Transfer Spar Max Impulse
problem_statement: Brittle transfer spar 2l=0.8m. supports at ends. Midpoint blow J at t=0. fractures instantly. halves mass m=0.25kg, length l=0.4m, wave speed c=160m/s. support spills if displacement > delta=1.0mm. What is max impulse J_max (N s) to avoid spilling before wavefront arrival?

name: Energy per Length dE/dL
problem_statement: Oscillator M2 (mass m) on frictionless rail connected to fixed M1 by spring (k, L). M3 (m) passes at y=0 with speed v0. sudden regime. m=0.2kg, k=0.08N/m, d=0.5m, v0=10m/s, M1=5e12kg. What is dE/dL at L=0 in J/m? (3 s.f.)

name: Spring Extension Rate
problem_statement: Two sleds (m1=0.3kg, m2=0.7kg) connected by spring k=50N/m. Forces applied in windows: Window 1 (t<T) F1=F, F2=4F. Window 2 (T<t<beta*T) F1=-2F, F2=gamma*F. F=4N, T=0.2s, beta=1.97, gamma=2.20813. Find spring extension rate q_dot (m/s) at the earliest time t* > beta*T when x_cm=0 and q=0 simultaneously.

name: Synthetic Gravity Impulse
problem_statement: Synthetic gravity G=12.0. m1=80kg (fixed), m2=1.60kg (on x-axis with spring k=2.0). m3=0.8kg passes along x=0 with v0=0.4m/s. d=0.3m. What is total oscillation energy E_osc in Joules (3 s.f.) long after m3 passes?

name: Calibration Boom Deflection
problem_statement: Thin elastic rod L=0.8m, rigidity k=12. rho(s)=0.5*e^(2.5s), a(s)=9+5s. Clamped at s=0. Tip (s=L) has Kt=180N/m and Kr=6Nm. What is the magnitude of the static tip deflection |y(L)| in mm? (3 s.f.)
